title: Verbs Whose Meaning Changes with Indicative or Subjunctive

sections.content:
You know the subjunctive after feelings (*Siento que no puedas venir*) from A2 Unit 27, reported orders (*Me dijo que cerrara la ventana*) from B1 Unit 38 and *sentir que* from B2 Unit 6. A core group of Spanish verbs change their meaning completely depending on whether the clause after *que* uses the indicative (stating or perceiving a fact) or the subjunctive (expressing a request, emotion, evaluation or consequence).

• *decir que*: + indicative = report a fact (*Dice que llueve*); + subjunctive = tell someone to do something (*Dice que vengas*).
• *sentir que*: + indicative = sense or perceive (*Siento que el contexto cambia*); + subjunctive = regret (*Siento que haya confusión*).
• *entender / comprender que*: + indicative = realise or grasp a fact (*Entiendo que la regla es explícita*); + subjunctive = find a reaction understandable (*Entiendo que estés molesto*).
• *temer(se) que*: + indicative = suspect an unwelcome fact, often with *me temo* (*Me temo que no hay entradas*); + subjunctive = fear something may happen (*Temo que surja un malentendido*).
• *suponer que*: + indicative = assume (*Supongo que ya lo sabes*); + subjunctive = imply or entail a consequence (*Eso supone que tengamos que revisar el texto*).

sections.title: Five double-mood verbs: indicative vs. subjunctive
rows: Dice que viene mañana. / Dice que vengas mañana.
Siento que algo falla. / Siento que no puedas venir.
Entiendo que el mensaje es claro. / Entiendo que dudes.
Me temo que ya cerraron. / Temo que se confundan.
Supongo que llegará pronto. / Eso supone que esperemos.

items.spanish: La directora dice que el cambio es explícito, pero también dice que revisemos el informe.
items.english: The director says the change is explicit, and she also tells us to review the report.

items.spanish: Siento que el mensaje implícito genera confusión; siento que no podamos aclararlo hoy.
items.english: I sense that the implicit message causes confusion; I am sorry that we cannot clarify it today.

items.spanish: Comprendo que la interpretación depende del contexto, y comprendo que te preocupes.
items.english: I realise that the interpretation depends on context, and I understand your being worried.

items.spanish: Supongo que aceptaron la suposición, aunque eso supone que cambiemos el plan.
items.english: I assume they accepted the assumption, although that entails our changing the plan.

sections.content: English uses different verbs (*say* vs. *tell*, *sense* vs. *be sorry*, *assume* vs. *entail*), while Spanish uses the same verb and lets the mood carry the meaning. Always ask whether the verb is stating information (indicative) or expressing an order, feeling, sympathy or consequence (subjunctive).
